claim: Analysis discovers concepts; design assigns responsibilities
counterexample: Premature implementation classes make the analysis model brittle; pure noun harvesting creates empty classes with no defensible responsibility.

claim: Software requirements need multiple kinds of precision
counterexample: An apparently atomic user story can hide several independent obligations and contradictory edge conditions.

claim: Use cases describe externally valuable behavior
counterexample: A use-case model without alternate flows gives designers no contract for recoverable failure.

claim: Class discovery turns language into relationships
counterexample: Choosing composition merely because one object references another can prohibit legitimate independent lifetimes.
Diagrams that show only successful synchronous calls conceal timing, retry and partial-failure semantics.

claim: State machines are executable constraints on lifecycles
counterexample: A “state” invented for every minor flag produces combinatorial explosion; too few states hide illegal behavior.

claim: Design is the distribution of responsibility
counterexample: Too many tiny interfaces can obscure responsibility just as a single god object does.

claim: A design sequence should be realizable
counterexample: Treating event publication as exactly-once without a precise end-to-end definition is a classic distributed design mistake.
Creating a factory, strategy and observer for a single immutable method needlessly multiplies code paths and tests.

claim: Constraints turn informal rules into testable predicates
counterexample: Formal-looking syntax may conceal incorrect scope, missing null cases and time-dependent assumptions.

claim: Persistence design is about identity and failure recovery
counterexample: Database schema diagram completeness is not evidence that concurrent operations preserve business rules.

claim: A defendable design is a consistent set of claims
counterexample: Diagrams may be internally consistent but still solve the wrong problem; revisit actor goals and original constraints.
